input.reasoning: Eight framings searched, including the negations of both the source wording and the proposed canonical, plus alternate vocabulary (compact stars, cosmic rays, particle colliders). The graph holds a small LHC-safety cluster, none of which is this proposition: (1) the parent conclusion "Collisions at the LHC present no danger" is broader and mechanism-neutral, resting on Hawking evaporation and other arguments as well, so identical decomposition fails; (2) "The LHC can create microscopic black holes" is the production possibility itself, and could be true alongside this claim if any produced holes evaporate; (3) "Natural cosmic-ray collisions on Earth have already produced the equivalent of the LHC's entire experimental program" is a sibling safety argument, but it turns on Earth's exposure rather than on the survival of dense stars, so different considerations bear on it; (4) the Hawking claims are an independent safety subclaim. Since the survival of white dwarfs and neutron stars under cosmic-ray bombardment is a distinct evidential basis, absent from the graph, the claim is new. The proposed canonical form is adopted: it is neutral, positive, mechanism-naming, and states the safety argument rather than its negation, so both the LSAG-affirming side and critics of the cosmic-ray argument would accept it as what is in dispute. The source sentence asserts this argument outright (it does not pose it as a question or merely report others' positions), so its instance affirms. Confidence is below 0.9 only because a counterpart phrased around the safety report or specific analysis without safety vocabulary could in principle have evaded embedding search.
input.direction_note: The discourse poses the safety argument affirmatively, as the debate motion "is the LHC safe"; the positive, mechanism-naming form is taken rather than a negated variant ("does not rule out"), and this source's first instance lands on the affirming side of that direction.
